mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.00% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to compressed discounting of future earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.00% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during confirmed tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 8.0% for two consecutive months coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightening reduces speculative positioning in equities.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >70% of such UNRATE moves, or IC < -0.10 over rolling 12-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private demand) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (inflation) by at least 2% in the prior quarter, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as outpacing demand inflation supports real earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥2% in prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such events, or IC > 0.10 over 6-month rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% while HOUST (retail sales) remains flat or rises is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary conditions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥3% while HOUST does not rise by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during confirmed contractionary cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as financial balance sheets signal risk aversion and capital inflows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of 4-month RSAFS declines, or IC < -0.05 over 1-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) exceeding 2% month-over-month coincides with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor demand crowds out equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during such spikes.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 growth exceeds CPIAUCSL by at least 1% but remains below 3%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as the signal of healthy but not excessive demand supports optimism.
candidate_trigger: 1% < (GDPC1 growth - CPIAUCSL growth) < 3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >75% of such events, or IC < -0.15 over 6-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to 'high inflation' as defined by CPIAUCSL > 220 in the prior month is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors preemptively reduce equity exposure amid expectations of tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 220 in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during confirmed high-inflation episodes.
